data.statement: Replace the deprecated stdlib audioop dependency in audio_assembly_service with an internal stdlib-only PCM codec (lin2lin, ratecv with state, tomono, tostereo for 1/2/3/4-byte samples), proven byte-exact against audioop by a differential test on Python 3.12, and raise requires-python from >=3.12,<3.13 to >=3.12,<3.14 so Audio Assembly and Scene Mix survive Python 3.13 where audioop was removed.

acceptance: No module under 04_Software/AudioMancer/src imports audioop any more.
A new internal PCM codec module exposes sample-width conversion, mono/stereo channel conversion, and stateful rate conversion for sample widths 1, 2, 3 and 4 bytes.
Codec sample-width conversion is byte-identical to audioop.lin2lin for every ordered width pair drawn from {1,2,3,4}.
Codec rate conversion returns bytes and carry-over state byte-identical to audioop.ratecv for representative rate pairs, including a stream fed in successive chunks where state carries across calls.
Codec mono-to-stereo is byte-identical to audioop.tostereo(data, width, 1.0, 1.0) and stereo-to-mono is byte-identical to audioop.tomono(data, width, 0.5, 0.5).
Channel conversion other than mono-to-stereo or stereo-to-mono still raises RuntimeError with the existing Audio Assembly message.
The differential comparison test skips cleanly instead of failing when audioop is unavailable, so the suite is green on Python 3.13.
pyproject requires-python is >=3.12,<3.14 and the configured test and lint gates pass on both Python 3.12 and Python 3.13.
Existing Audio Assembly and Scene Mix tests, including final assembly WAV parameter conversion, still pass unchanged.
assumptions: The new codec replicates audioop semantics exactly rather than WAV-standard semantics; in particular audioop treats 1-byte samples as signed, so the codec does too, preserving current behaviour bit-for-bit.

audioop.ratecv linear-interpolation resampling and its (weights, previous-sample) state tuple can be reproduced deterministically in pure Python; the differential test is the proof, not the assumption.
Raising the pin to <3.14 only widens the accepted interpreter range; no dependency version is changed, and PySide6>=6.8 already supports Python 3.13.
open_questions: Approve proceeding at risk level medium? The change rewrites PCM audio conversion maths that every produced audiobook passes through, and widens the supported interpreter range.
data.reason: Policy requires pause at risk threshold medium. Both design questions are already answered by the user (internal stdlib codec; raise pin to <3.14); what remains is explicit human approval of the medium risk before requirement and implementation work begins.
recommended_responses: Approve. The differential oracle test compares the new codec byte-for-byte against the audioop implementation it replaces, so a silent audio regression fails the suite rather than shipping, and the pin raise is validated on a real local 3.13 interpreter.
scope: IN: new internal PCM codec module under src/audiomancer; removal of the audioop import and its four call sites in audio_assembly_service.py; unit + differential tests for the codec; requires-python raised to >=3.12,<3.14 and ruff target-version reviewed; component documentation for the new module. OUT: any change to Audio Assembly behaviour, settings, report format or public service API; support for compressed/non-PCM WAV; sample widths outside 1/2/3/4; adding numpy or audioop-lts as a dependency; upgrading or re-pinning any third-party dependency.
data.source: User chat ticket: '2. audioop - eliminat in Python 3.13 (portabilitate in timp)'. User decisions: internal stdlib PCM codec (not audioop-lts, not numpy); raise the Python pin in this same change.
data.understanding: audio_assembly_service.py currently imports the stdlib audioop module and uses lin2lin, ratecv, tomono and tostereo to convert PCM WAV frame chunks between sample widths, sample rates and mono/stereo layouts during final assembly and Scene Mix. audioop was removed in Python 3.13, so the requires-python pin >=3.12,<3.13 is the only thing hiding a hard breakage. This change extracts the PCM conversion into a new internal stdlib-only module (no third-party dependency, no numpy) that reimplements exactly the four operations for 1/2/3/4-byte samples, rewires audio_assembly_service to call it instead of audioop, and raises requires-python to >=3.12,<3.14. Behaviour must be preserved byte-for-byte, which is proven by a differential test that compares the new codec against real audioop while running on Python 3.12 and skips cleanly on 3.13+ where audioop no longer exists.

Performance measured: the stdlib codec is 89x to 210x slower than the C audioop it replaces (30s of 44100Hz 16-bit stereo: sample-width 0.003s vs 0.717s, stereo-to-mono 0.004s vs 0.577s, resample 0.013s vs 1.164s). Absolute cost is 0.04s CPU per second of audio resampled, about 23 minutes for a 10-hour audiobook. The unconverted fast path where source and target WAV parameters already match is unaffected because it copies frames without touching the codec.

data.rationale: Audio Assembly must retarget source WAV sample width without altering produced audio after audioop was removed from the standard library.
data.requirement: The PCM codec shall convert linear PCM sample data between 1, 2, 3 and 4 byte sample widths by arithmetic bit shift, producing bytes identical to the removed audioop.lin2lin.
data.verification: Automated: golden vectors plus byte-exact differential comparison against audioop for every ordered width pair from {1,2,3,4}.

data.rationale: Scene Mix and final assembly must retarget channel layout without altering produced audio after audioop was removed from the standard library.
data.requirement: The PCM codec shall convert linear PCM sample data between mono and stereo channel layouts using clipped floor arithmetic identical to the removed audioop.tostereo and audioop.tomono.
data.verification: Automated: golden floor/clip vectors plus byte-exact differential comparison against audioop.tostereo and audioop.tomono.

data.rationale: Final assembly streams WAV data in chunks, so resampling must stay continuous across chunk boundaries without altering produced audio.
data.requirement: The PCM codec shall resample linear PCM sample data between sample rates while threading carry-over state across successive chunks, producing bytes and state identical to the removed audioop.ratecv.
data.verification: Automated: byte-exact differential comparison of bytes and carry-over state against audioop.ratecv across five rate pairs, both channel counts and a chunked stream.

data.rationale: An unsupported width must fail loudly at the conversion boundary rather than emitting silently corrupted audio.
data.requirement: The PCM codec shall raise ValueError when asked to operate on a sample width outside 1, 2, 3 and 4 bytes.
data.verification: Automated: 2 linked pytest selectors covering unsupported widths and non-positive channel/rate values.

data.rationale: A stream may begin with or contain an empty chunk, which must not corrupt resampler state or raise.
data.requirement: The PCM codec shall return empty output for empty input, and rate conversion shall still return a usable carry-over state.
data.verification: Automated: empty-input case asserted for all four sample widths across every conversion.

data.rationale: Unsupported channel layouts must be refused explicitly; this pre-existing contract must survive the move off audioop.
data.requirement: Audio Assembly shall raise RuntimeError when a WAV channel conversion other than mono to stereo or stereo to mono is required.
data.verification: Automated: RuntimeError message asserted for a 3-to-2 channel conversion.

data.rationale: audioop has no stdlib replacement, so any remaining import makes Audio Assembly and Scene Mix fail at import time on Python 3.13.
data.requirement: No AudioMancer source module shall depend on the audioop standard-library module removed in Python 3.13.
data.verification: Automated: source tree scanned for audioop imports; also confirmed by importing audio_assembly_service on Python 3.13.

data.rationale: The range must admit Python 3.13 once the audioop blocker is gone, while keeping 3.14 an explicit future decision rather than an accident.
data.requirement: The AudioMancer package shall declare its supported interpreter range as Python 3.12 up to but excluding 3.14.
data.verification: Automated: pyproject requires-python parsed and asserted equal to >=3.12,<3.14.

data.rationale: The oracle comparison can only run where audioop still exists, so the suite must stay green on Python 3.13 without losing the check on 3.12.
data.requirement: The PCM codec differential parity test shall skip rather than fail when the audioop reference module is unavailable.
data.verification: Automated: parity guard asserted to track interpreter version so the suite stays green on 3.13.
